propositions: Hand-rolled CLI argument parsing in claim.py and transition.py must be refactored to use Python's stdlib argparse while preserving all observable behavior and load-bearing sentinel semantics (None vs empty-string for --assignee, command-specific --force token consumption rules).

The --force flag has command-specific semantics that must be preserved: in claim, bare --force consumes the following non-option token as reason (else '(no reason given)'); in transition, bare --force sets force_reason='' (not consuming following tokens) and force_reason is None only when absent.

The --assignee flag must preserve its None-vs-empty-string distinction: absent invokes default_assignee fallback, explicit --assignee '' clears the assignee, and value-less --assignee exits with code 1.

The transition._parse_flags private function is directly imported and called by three external tests expecting an exact 5-tuple return (reason, force_reason, close_class, caused_by, ref) with specific None/empty semantics; it must be retained as an argparse-backed shim.

Unknown/extra tokens must be silently skipped, partial flag abbreviations must not match, --help must remain dispatcher-served byte-exact from golden help files, and the retired --force-close flag must reject with exit code 1 and a specific message.
